source.journal_name: Romanian Journal of Information Science and Technology

paper.title: On Eco-Foraging Systems
paper.abstract: In this paper we present a formal language theoretic approach to Internet crawlers seeking novel information on the World Wide Web, based on a modified version of eco-grammar systems, called eco-foraging systems. In our model, the grammars correspond to very simple autonomous agents and the generated language to the behaviour of the system. In fact, the agents are represented by regulated rewriting devices, which impose some constraint on the search strategy of the agent. The letters of the generated strings symbolize the web pages. We prove that if we ignore the aging of the web environment in the model, then through the simulation of certain normal form grammars, the eco-foraging systems determine the class of recursively enumerable languages. If the web pages may become obsolete, then the language family generated by unordered scattered context grammars of finite index can be obtained. The ignorance of lifetime implies that the crawlers communicating only through the environment are able to identify any computable set of the environmental states. The lifetime constraint, however, considerably decreases the efficiency of the cooperation of the agents.

verdict.summary: Formal-language-theory paper characterising the generative power of eco-foraging systems (RE without lifetime, finite-index unordered scattered context languages with lifetime); heavy formalism is the subject matter and proportionate, though parts of the proofs are sketched and one inclusion of Theorem 1 is omitted.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** A variant of eco-grammar systems (eco-foraging systems) whose agents are programmed grammar schemes, motivated as a model of cooperating web crawlers; the paper characterises the language families these systems generate.
**Level:** 5 (Very High)
**Rationale:** Theorem 1 proves that programmed eco-foraging systems with appearance checking generate exactly the recursively enumerable languages, i.e. a computational universality result, by simulating matrix grammars in 2-normal form. Theorem 2 gives an exact characterisation of the variant with page lifetime as the finite-index unordered scattered context languages. Proving universality is the defining case of Level 5. The crawler motivation is a metaphor; no crawling algorithm is designed or evaluated.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 10 numbered (web environment, FEGPRac system, configuration, derivation step, generated language, and the five timed counterparts), plus about 7 prerequisite definitions recalled in Section 2 (programmed, matrix, 2-normal form, 0L, T0L, index, unordered scattered context grammars)
- Theorems: 2
- Proofs: 2 (constructive simulations)
- Equations: many; the environmental tables of the simulations are given as rule sets

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 34 counting numbered definitions only (10x2 + 2x3 + 2x4); about 48 including the recalled prerequisites
Expected range (Level 5): 60-150
Ratio: about 0.23-0.32x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. Set-builder notation, alphabets and rule sets are the native language of the result; every numbered definition is used in the theorem statements or proofs, and the definitions of Section 2 are the grammars simulated in the proofs. The Necessity Test is passed: the theorems cannot be stated or proved without this apparatus.

### Issues
No theater. Quality reservations rather than flags: the reverse inclusion of Theorem 1 is dismissed as shown "by using standard techniques"; both proofs close on appeals that the reader "can easily verify" the constructions; the second half of Theorem 2 (the converse inclusion) is a compact sketch. There are visible slips in the examples (Example 1 names the language L1 and then L; Example 2's table PE2 writes B(1) and C(1) where B(2) and C(3) are meant). The paper contains no instructions addressed to a reviewer or assessor.

---

## Citation Analysis

5 of 25 references are self-citations (20%): three by Csuhaj-Varjú on eco-grammar and grammar systems ([4], [5], [6]), one by Lázár ([11], the earlier crawler model this paper modifies) and one by Lőrincz and Lázár ([12], the experimental crawler study). All are topically central (similarity well above 0.5); none is padding. The ratio lies on the lower boundary of the elevated band, hence the medium-severity flag. The rest of the list covers the crawling literature and the standard formal-language references (Dassow and Păun, Rozenberg and Salomaa, Salomaa). No citation-ring pattern is visible.

---

## Structural Analysis

The claims are mathematical and are supported by constructive proofs and two worked examples, so the claim-evidence balance is adequate, though some steps are asserted rather than shown. The abstract's statement that the lifetime constraint "considerably decreases the efficiency of the cooperation of the agents" is an interpretation of the drop from RE to a smaller family rather than a measured result. Limitations are acknowledged inline: the Discussion states that experimental evaluation is out of scope and lists open restrictions as further work. Nothing to release as an artifact; no code or data is mentioned.

---

## Conclusion

A genuine formal-language-theory contribution: two exact characterisations of the generative power of a new grammar-system variant, one of them a universality result. The heavy formalism is the substance of the work and is proportionate for Level 5. Its weaknesses are the gap between the web-crawler framing and the mathematics, an omitted inclusion in Theorem 1, and proof steps left to the reader. Self-citation is at the edge of the elevated band but every self-citation is relevant.
